title: Text files and paths
subtitle: Variables disappear when a program ends. Save data to a file to read it next time.
concept: Variables disappear when a program ends. Save data to a file to read it next time.
intuition: Write today's list on paper so you can read it tomorrow.
objectives: Specify the file mode and text encoding
Reading a file still gives text

body.title: Choose where to write
body.text: notes.txt is a filename. Without a full path, it is relative to the program's current working directory, which may differ from the code directory. Start in a separate practice folder. The web replay uses an isolated example directory and does not write files on your computer.

body.title: Specify the file mode and text encoding
body.text: with open("notes.txt", "w", encoding="utf-8") as file: opens a file for writing. Mode w truncates an existing file, so practice with a new filename. The encoding determines how text is stored; this book consistently uses UTF-8. file.write("Buy apples\n") writes text; \n is a newline. with closes the file when its indented block ends.

body.title: Reading a file still gives text
body.text: Open the same file in r mode. text = file.read() reads its contents as a string. Use print(text, end="") to preserve the file's newlines without adding another one. Mode a appends to existing content; check the destination first.

formalDefinition.text: with open(...) opens a file and closes it at the end of the block. r reads, w overwrites, and a appends.
conditions: w overwrites an existing file. Use new filenames in a separate practice directory.
Relative paths start at the current working directory. Use UTF-8 consistently when reading and writing.

derivation.text: w creates or overwrites the example file and writes a line.
The file closes when the with block ends.
r reopens it to read and display the saved text.

interactiveVisual.prediction: Does text change when it is written to a file and read back?
interactiveVisual.caption: Choose an input and predict the result, then select Next step. The arrow marks the next statement to execute; the side panel shows current variables and output produced so far.

experiment.code:
message = 'Buy apples'
with open("notes.txt", "w", encoding="utf-8") as file:
    file.write(message)
with open("notes.txt", "r", encoding="utf-8") as file:
    text = file.read()
print(text)

interactiveVisual.followUp: Try empty text and inspect text after reading. Each replay starts in a fresh example directory.

workedExamples.title: Save a note
workedExamples.problem: Write Buy apples, close the file, then read it again.
steps: w creates or overwrites the example file and writes a line.
The file closes when the with block ends.
r reopens it to read and display the saved text.

answer.code:
with open("notes.txt", "w", encoding="utf-8") as file:
    file.write("Buy apples\n")
with open("notes.txt", "r", encoding="utf-8") as file:
    text = file.read()
print(text, end="")

workedExamples.title: Append at the end
workedExamples.problem: Keep the first line and add a second with a.
steps: a preserves the existing content and writes at the end.
Reading the file returns both lines.

answer.code:
with open("notes.txt", "w", encoding="utf-8") as file:
    file.write("Buy apples\n")
with open("notes.txt", "a", encoding="utf-8") as file:
    file.write("Buy bread\n")
with open("notes.txt", "r", encoding="utf-8") as file:
    text = file.read()
print(text, end="")

commonMistakes.correction: w truncates the file. Use a to append.

commonMistakes.claim: A relative path always starts at the code file's directory.
commonMistakes.correction: It starts at the current working directory. Check where the program is running.

practice.problem: Write Hello to a new hello.txt, then read it.
practice.hint: After writing, open it in r mode.
solution: Use the same UTF-8 encoding for writing and reading.

answer.code:
with open("hello.txt", "w", encoding="utf-8") as file:
    file.write("Hello")
with open("hello.txt", "r", encoding="utf-8") as file:
    text = file.read()
print(text)

practice.problem: Append B to an example file containing A.
solution: Write A first, then append B.

answer.code:
with open("letters.txt", "w", encoding="utf-8") as file:
    file.write("A")
with open("letters.txt", "a", encoding="utf-8") as file:
    file.write("B")
with open("letters.txt", "r", encoding="utf-8") as file:
    text = file.read()
print(text)

practice.problem: Overwrite A with B using w in an example file.
practice.hint: Reopening with w discards the old content.

answer.code:
with open("letters.txt", "w", encoding="utf-8") as file:
    file.write("A")
with open("letters.txt", "w", encoding="utf-8") as file:
    file.write("B")
with open("letters.txt", "r", encoding="utf-8") as file:
    text = file.read()
print(text)

practice.problem: What is the length of the text read from an empty example file?

answer.code:
with open("empty.txt", "w", encoding="utf-8") as file:
    file.write("")
with open("empty.txt", "r", encoding="utf-8") as file:
    text = file.read()
print(len(text))

learningCheck.question: Which mode preserves content and adds at the end?
learningCheck.explanation: a appends, w overwrites, and r reads.
feedback: w discards existing content, so it cannot preserve it here.
Yes. a appends after the existing content.
r is a read mode and cannot write.
